What are the $x$-intercepts of the parabola shown above?
after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(3,-4)$ and passes through the point $(0,-\frac{7}{4}).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(3,-4)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4p(y+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(0,-\frac{7}{4}),$ we substitute $x=0$ and $y=-\frac{7}{4}$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-3)^{2} & =4p(-\frac{7}{4}+4) \\ 9 & =4p(\frac{9}{4}) \\ p & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4(y+4).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4(0+4) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =16 \\ x-3 & =\pm 4 \\ x & =\pm 4+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts are $7$ and $-1.$

after.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(-5,-6)$ and passes through the point $(-1,2).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(-5,-6)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)^{2} & =4p(y+6).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-1,2),$ we substitute $x=-1$ and $y=2$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1+5)^{2} & =4p(2+6) \\ 16 & =4p(8) \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)^{2} & =2(y+6).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)^{2} & =2(0+6) \\ (x+5)^{2} & =12 \\ x+5 & =\pm \sqrt{12} \\ x & =\pm 2\sqrt{3}-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts are $\pm 2\sqrt{3}-5.$

First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(4,-3)$ and passes through the point $(10,6).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(4,-3)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-4)^{2}=4p(y+3).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(10,6),$ we substitute $x=10$ and $y=6$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(10-4)^{2} & =4p(6+3) \\ 36 & =4p(9) \\ p & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =4(y+3).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-4)^{2} & =4(y+3) \\ 16 & =4(y+3) \\ 4 & =y+3 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $1.$
